stem:
A student investigated the effect of sucrose concentration on the mass of potato tissue.

1. A 1.0 mol dm⁻³ sucrose solution was diluted with distilled water to give 20 cm³ of each concentration shown in the table, in labelled boiling tubes.
2. Eighteen cylinders were cut from one potato with a cork borer and trimmed to 30 mm with a scalpel on a tile.
3. Each cylinder was blotted, weighed and placed in a tube (three cylinders per concentration).
4. After 60 minutes at room temperature, each cylinder was removed, blotted and reweighed.

The results (initial mass → final mass, in g) were:

| Sucrose concentration / mol dm⁻³ | Cylinder 1 | Cylinder 2 | Cylinder 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.00 | 1.52 → 1.71 | 1.48 → 1.66 | 1.55 → 1.75 |
| 0.15 | 1.50 → 1.58 | 1.47 → 1.55 | 1.53 → 1.62 |
| 0.30 | 1.49 → 1.43 | 1.54 → 1.48 | 1.51 → 1.45 |
| 0.45 | 1.53 → 1.37 | 1.50 → 1.48 | 1.46 → 1.31 |
| 0.60 | 1.48 → 1.28 | 1.52 → 1.31 | 1.50 → 1.30 |
| 0.75 | 1.51 → 1.25 | 1.49 → 1.24 | 1.54 → 1.28 |

parts.label: (i)

accepted.value: the concentration of the sucrose solution

parts.explanation: The student varied the sucrose concentration.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.stem: State the dependent variable and how it should be expressed.

points.description: Change in mass of the potato cylinders, expressed as percentage change in mass

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The change in mass of the cylinders, expressed as percentage change in mass.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.stem: State two variables that were standardised in this method.

points.description: Volume of solution (20 cm³) / time in solution (60 minutes)
Length or diameter of cylinders / same potato / temperature (room temperature)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The volume of solution (20 cm³) and the time in the solution (60 minutes); also the length and diameter of the cylinders, which all came from one potato.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Complete the proportional dilution for 20 cm³ of 0.45 mol dm⁻³ sucrose.

payload.template: Volume of 1.0 mol dm⁻³ sucrose = {{blank:s}} cm³; volume of distilled water = {{blank:w}} cm³.

parts.explanation: $0.45 / 1.0 \times 20 = 9\ \text{cm}^3$ of stock, made up to 20 cm³ with $11\ \text{cm}^3$ of water.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Describe how the student should set out a table to record the raw and processed results.

points.description: Independent variable (sucrose concentration / mol dm⁻³) in the first column
Column headings with units in the heading only (e.g. initial mass / g, final mass / g, percentage change in mass / %), not in the cells
Columns for each replicate and for the mean; masses to the same number of decimal places (2 d.p.)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The first column would show sucrose concentration / mol dm⁻³. Further columns would show initial mass / g and final mass / g for each of the three cylinders, then percentage change in mass / % for each and the mean percentage change. Units appear only in the headings, and all masses are recorded to two decimal places.

parts.label: (i)
parts.stem: Calculate the percentage change in mass of cylinder 2 in 0.60 mol dm⁻³ sucrose, to one decimal place. Include a minus sign for a loss.

parts.label: (ii)

options.rationale: Correct: it lost only about 1% while the other two lost about 10%.
Its gain (12.5%) is close to the other two in water.
Its loss (about 17%) matches the other two.
Its gain (about 5%) matches the other two.

parts.explanation: 1.50 → 1.48 g is a change of about −1.3%, far from the −10.5% and −10.3% of the other cylinders.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.stem: Calculate the mean percentage change in mass in 0.45 mol dm⁻³ sucrose, leaving out the anomalous result. Give your answer to one decimal place.
parts.explanation: Cylinder 1: $−10.46\%$; cylinder 3: $−10.27\%$. Mean $= −10.4\%$. Including the anomaly gives $−7.4\%$.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Cylinder 1: $−10.46\%$; cylinder 3: $−10.27\%$. Mean $= −10.4\%$. Including the anomaly gives $−7.4\%$.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: The mean percentage changes (leaving out the anomaly) are 12.5, 5.6, −4.0, −10.4, −13.6, −17.0 for 0.00 to 0.75 mol dm⁻³. Describe the graph of mean percentage change in mass against concentration.

points.description: Percentage change decreases as concentration increases: gain at low concentrations, loss at high
Line crosses zero between 0.15 and 0.30 mol dm⁻³; steep fall at first, becoming less steep above 0.45 mol dm⁻³ (levelling)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: As sucrose concentration increases, the percentage change falls from a gain of 12.5% in water to a loss of 17.0% at 0.75 mol dm⁻³. The line crosses zero between 0.15 and 0.30 mol dm⁻³, and the fall becomes less steep at the highest concentrations.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: Using the means at 0.15 mol dm⁻³ (+5.55%) and 0.30 mol dm⁻³ (−3.97%), and assuming a straight line between them, estimate the sucrose concentration that would cause no change in mass. Give your answer to two decimal places.

parts.label: (g)
parts.stem: Explain what the concentration in (f) tells you about the potato cells.

points.description: At this concentration there is no net movement of water by osmosis
So the water potential of the solution equals the water potential of the potato cells / tissue

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: At about 0.24 mol dm⁻³ there is no net gain or loss of water by osmosis, so this solution has the same water potential as the potato cells.

parts.label: (h)
parts.stem: Identify one source of systematic error and one source of random error in this method.

points.description: Systematic: e.g. balance not zeroed / incorrectly calibrated (all masses shifted), or evaporation of water from all tubes
Random: e.g. blotting removed different amounts of surface liquid / cylinders cut to slightly different sizes / cylinders not fully submerged

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A systematic error would be a balance that was not zeroed, shifting every mass by the same amount. A random error would be blotting the cylinders inconsistently, so different amounts of surface solution remained.

parts.label: (i)
parts.stem: Suggest three improvements to the method that would increase confidence in the estimate.

points.description: More concentrations between 0.15 and 0.30 mol dm⁻³ (smaller intervals near the zero point)
More replicates (e.g. five per concentration) and calculate means / repeat the anomalous result
Standardise blotting (same number of rolls on the same paper) / control temperature with a water bath / leave longer to reach equilibrium / cover tubes

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Use more concentrations between 0.15 and 0.30 mol dm⁻³, for example every 0.03 mol dm⁻³; use five cylinders per concentration and repeat any anomalous result; and standardise blotting and control the temperature with a thermostatically controlled water bath, leaving the cylinders long enough to reach a steady mass.

parts.label: (j)
parts.stem: Assess the overall risk of this investigation and state one precaution.

points.description: Low risk; e.g. cut away from the body with the scalpel / cork borer onto a tile

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Low risk. Cut with the scalpel and cork borer away from the body, onto a tile.

explanation: Percentage change in mass falls with sucrose concentration; the tissue's water potential equals that of about 0.24 mol dm⁻³ sucrose.
hints: For a proportional dilution, volume of stock = required concentration ÷ stock concentration × total volume.
